correctness.rationale: The first three order conditions give mean 1/2 and variance 1/12 at two distinct sorted nodes, and c in [0,1] gives u in [1/6,1/2]. Independently, in the B-orthonormal basis (1, sqrt(12)(c-1/2)), the matrix A has first column (1/2,1/sqrt(12)) and upper-right entry -1/sqrt(12) by the remaining order condition. In that basis the algebraic-stability form is diagonal with entries 0 and twice the lower-right entry of A, so that entry is t/6 for arbitrary t>=0. This is reversible and verifies exhaustiveness. The scalar test function in this basis gives the stated numerator and denominator, and residual |1-t|/(1+t) without a degenerate leading denominator. The upper-right Butcher-entry depth is strictly positive and strictly increasing in t at every u; at the least feasible t=(1-rho)/(1+rho) the other entries are positive. The derivative of the remaining depth function in u is strictly increasing for u>1/6, and its boundary signs are (3t-1)/8 and (5+t)/8. This proves attainment, the change at rho=1/2, the root characterization, and uniqueness including the equality case at the transition. Independently checked the exact Radau IIA tableau and sampled depths 1/12, 1/18, 0.04503467712462134 at rho=0,1/2,3/4, and the limit 0.03563906993888331.
residual_risks: Sampled depths are corroboration; the all-budget result and uniqueness use the analytic argument.
No claim for other numbers of stages, unbounded nodes, or nonlinear SSP or finite-step objectives.

value.rationale: Stiff-limit damping and the size of negative Butcher entries are natural, distinct design constraints. The exact Pareto profile supplies a uniquely determined tableau for each budget and a nonobvious change from an endpoint node to two interior nodes at rho=1/2. This information is useful even knowing both the classical zero-residual tableau and the old unconstrained minimum; it is not an SSP or finite-step optimality theorem.
residual_risks: Design interpretation is restricted to the stated two-stage class and scalar stiff limit.
